meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking a direct object.

examples.text: لازم نختبر حرارة الفرن قبل ما ندخل الصينية.
examples.trans: We need to test the oven temperature before putting the tin in.

examples.text: مازن بختبر كل وصفة بدقة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Mazen tests every recipe with great precision.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Heavy in weight, or sometimes heavy-blooded (annoying/dull person).

examples.text: هذا الصندوق الثقيل ما بقدر أرفعه.
examples.trans: I cannot lift this heavy box.

examples.text: هالكرسي الحديد الثقيل بده اتنين يحملوه.
examples.trans: This heavy iron chair takes two people to carry it.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: On Friday, the whole family gathers.

examples.text: بنزور ستي كل يوم الجمعة بعد صلاة الظهر.
examples.trans: We visit my grandmother every Friday after the noon prayer.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.trans: Our weekend is on Saturday.

examples.text: يوم السبت الصبح دايماً بنروح نجيب خضرة من السوق.
examples.trans: On Saturday morning we always go buy vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: Used for shade from the sun.

examples.trans: Let's sit in the shade.

examples.text: صفينا السيارة تحت الشجرة عشان تضل في الظل.
examples.trans: We parked the car under the tree so it would stay in the shade.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Star.

examples.trans: The star shines in the sky.

examples.text: البنت لقت النجمة اللامعة بالسما ورتها لأخوها.
examples.trans: The girl spotted the bright star in the sky and showed it to her brother.

meanings.note: The left direction or side.

examples.trans: Turn left after the traffic light.

examples.text: باب الصيدلية على إيدك اليسار أول ما تفوت المجمع.
examples.trans: The pharmacy door is on your left as soon as you enter the complex.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: The kids are playing outside.

examples.text: الأولاد بلعبوا برا بالساحة جنب الشجر.
examples.trans: The children are playing outside in the courtyard beside the trees.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بسطات.

examples.trans: Turn left at the stair landing.
The landing is wide and bright.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for a balcony or veranda.

examples.text: شربنا القهوة عالبلكونة الخشب الطابق التاني.
examples.trans: We drank coffee on the wooden balcony on the second floor.
The balcony of Jasmine House overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The table is made of oak wood.
Oak trees are old and strong.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Active participle of the geminate verb تمّ.

examples.text: التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: A proper tasting requires complete silence in the kitchen.

examples.text: كلامك إله معنى تام ومقنع كتير.
examples.trans: Your words make total sense and are very convincing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: The feminine form of the Levantine possessive marker.

examples.trans: Reem's bag is lost.

examples.text: العلبة تبعت الشاي الأخضر عالرف التاني.
examples.trans: The green tea tin is on the second shelf.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for waiting for someone or something.

examples.trans: You must wait your turn in line.

examples.text: لازم تستنى شوي قبل ما تقطع الكيكة السخنة.
examples.trans: You have to wait a little before slicing the hot cake.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: I have nine books on the shelf.

examples.text: الساعة تسعة الصبح رح نلتقي عند النافورة.
examples.trans: At nine in the morning we will meet by the fountain.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Common Levantine Arabic verb meaning 'to expect', with feminine ending -i.

examples.trans: Do you think it's going to rain tomorrow?

examples.text: ما توقّعت أبداً أشوفك هون اليوم!
examples.trans: I never expected to see you here today!

meanings.note: Standard noun used in Jordanian for tree trunks and stems.

examples.text: في حلقة حديد معلقة على جذع الشجرة.
examples.trans: There is an iron ring hanging on the tree trunk.

examples.text: جذع شجرة البلوط قديم وعريض كتير.
examples.trans: The trunk of the oak tree is very old and wide.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: Refers to both weather and the emotional vibe of a room (ألطف الجو 'lighten the mood').

examples.trans: The mood is a bit tense today.
The weather is nice in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (plural: جيوب). Also homographic with imperative جيب ('bring!') from جاب.

examples.trans: The key is inside the jacket pocket.
I put the small watch in my pocket.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: The metal iron. Used commonly in construction contexts or metaphorically for strength.

examples.trans: This door is made of iron.

examples.text: قفل البوابة مصنوع من حديد قديم وتقيل.
examples.trans: The gate lock is made of old, heavy iron.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حلقات.

examples.trans: The brass ring is twenty millimetres wide.
We fitted a new washer on the pipe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.text: افتح الخريطة على التلفون عشان ما نضيع.
examples.trans: Open the map on the phone so we don't get lost.
We followed the blue lines on the old map.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: This table is made of wood.

examples.text: الصندوق مصنوع من خشب جوز قديم وناعم.
examples.trans: The chest is made of smooth old walnut wood.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a wooden or iron railing.

examples.trans: The balcony railing is made of oak wood.
Hold the banister as you go down the stairs.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Form II verb; commonly paired with النظر (to look closely / squint).

examples.text: دقق النظر تحت درابزين البلكونة يا طارق.
examples.trans: Look closely under the balcony railing, Tariq.

examples.text: مازن بدقق بكل تفاصيل الوصفة قبل الحكم.
examples.trans: Mazen scrutinizes every detail of the recipe before judging.

meanings.note: Active participle of رسم used as an agent noun (compare رسّام).

examples.text: ملاحظة راسم الخريطة مكتوبة على جنب الكرت.
examples.trans: The mapmaker's note is written on the side of the card.

examples.text: راسم اللوحة وقع اسمه بالزاوية التحتانية.
examples.trans: The drawer of the painting signed his name in the bottom corner.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ربيع (spring).

examples.text: اليوم في هبات هوا ربيعية نشطة بالبلد.
examples.trans: Today there are brisk spring wind gusts in town.

examples.text: الجو الربيعي بخلي القعدة بالساحة بتجنن.
examples.trans: The spring weather makes sitting in the courtyard wonderful.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: A noun referring to a single drawing, illustration, or painting.

examples.trans: This drawing is very beautiful.

examples.text: في رسمة صغيرة لورقة زيزفون على الهامش.
examples.trans: There is a small drawing of a linden leaf in the margin.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سلالم.

examples.trans: He played the musical scale slowly.
He climbed the ladder to fit the bulb.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Active participle of شاف ('to see'), standard in Jordanian for 'I see / do you see?'.

examples.text: شايفة رسمة المفتاح الدهبي فوق الباب!
examples.trans: I see the painted golden key above the door!
Do you see the yellow light in the attic window?

meanings.note: Form I transitive verb taking the thing resembled directly without a preposition.

examples.trans: This cup looks like my grandmother's cup.
The two boys resemble each other in their laugh.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.trans: We planted an olive tree in the garden.

examples.text: قعدنا تحت شجرة الزيزفون الكبيرة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We sat under the big linden tree in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: شو المكون السري اللي ضفتيه عالعجينة؟
examples.trans: What is the secret ingredient that you added to the batter?

meanings.note: Colloquial Form II verb adapted from English check; conjugated regularly as a medial weak Form II stem.

examples.text: شيّك عالساعة قبل ما تدخل المخبز.
examples.trans: Check the clock before you go into the bakery.

examples.text: سلمى شيّكت على كل البطاقات اللي بالعلبة.
examples.trans: Salma checked all the cards that were in the box.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

ضرب.gloss: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow

meanings.en: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow
meanings.note: Basic meaning 'to hit'. In everyday Jordanian a fuse or a machine 'hits' when it blows or fails (الفيوز ضرب 'the fuse blew').

examples.trans: The ball hit the window.

examples.text: الفيوز ضرب لما شغلنا الفرن والغسالة مع بعض.
examples.trans: The fuse blew when we ran the oven and the washing machine together.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the word for light.

examples.trans: Turn off the light before you sleep.

examples.text: ضو الفانوس الأصفر كشف الكتابة الباهتة.
examples.trans: The yellow lantern light revealed the faded writing.

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: Put the things on the table.

examples.text: طاولة المطبخ مليانة علب بهارات ومرطبانات.
examples.trans: The kitchen table is full of spice tins and jars.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: The music volume is very high.

examples.text: الرف العالي بالخزانة عليه كتب جدتي.
examples.trans: The high shelf in the cupboard holds my grandmother's books.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: المخبز بشتغل بنفس الوصفة من عشرين سنة.
examples.trans: The bakery has been using the same recipe for twenty years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.en: knot tied in rope or string
meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural عقد) from عقد ('to tie'). Used for literal rope knots and figurative complications.

examples.text: ربطت الحبل بعقدة مزدوجة عشان يثبت.
examples.trans: I tied the rope with a double knot so it stays firm.

examples.text: فكّينا العقدة بسهولة قبل ما الهوا يشد.
examples.trans: We untied the knot easily before the wind picked up.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means both a stone/wooden architectural pillar and a vertical column in a ledger or timetable.

examples.text: قرا مازن العمود التاني بالدفتر بدون نظارة.
examples.trans: Mazen read the second column in the notebook without glasses.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس جنب عمود الحجر بالساحة.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern beside the stone pillar in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The book is on top of the table.

examples.text: الخريطة معلقة فوق الرف الخشبي بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: The map is hanging above the wooden shelf in the library.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: This chair is not comfortable.

examples.text: جدي قعد على كرسي القش جنب شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: My grandfather sat on the wicker chair beside the lemon tree.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Jordanian Arabic word meaning 'then' or 'well then!'.

examples.text: مو حابب تشرب شاي؟ لعاد شو أعملك؟
examples.trans: You don't feel like drinking tea? Well then, what should I make you?

examples.text: الباص راح علينا، لعاد خلينا ناخد تاكسي.
examples.trans: We missed the bus—in that case, let's take a taxi.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبينة, plural: مبينين).

examples.trans: The wooden train looks old and precious.
It looks like it is going to rain tonight.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Feminine متينة, plural متان. Used for strong rope, thick paper, or solid construction.

examples.text: لازمنا حبل متين يتحمل وزن الفوانيس.
examples.trans: We need a sturdy rope that can bear the weight of the lanterns.
The cardboard is sturdy and doesn't tear easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مربوطة, plural: مربوطين).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag tied to the handle.
The red ribbon is tied securely.

meanings.note: Passive participle of طرق (to hammer or tread); refers to hammered brass/copper crafts or a frequently walked path.

examples.text: الصينية مصنوعة من نحاس مطروق بإيد حرفي.
examples.trans: The tray is made of hammered copper crafted by an artisan.

examples.text: هادا الدرب مطروق كتير بين السوق والمكتبة.
examples.trans: This path is well-trodden between the market and the library.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Masculine participle from علّق ('to hang'), meaning 'hung up' or 'hanging'.

examples.text: البرواز القديم معلّق عالحيط فوق البيانو.
examples.trans: The old frame is hanging on the wall above the piano.

examples.text: المعطف معلّق ورا الباب عشان ما ينسى ياخده معه.
examples.trans: The coat is hung behind the door so he doesn't forget to take it with him.

meanings.note: Defective noun on the maf'al pattern from عنى; plural معاني.

examples.text: هلق فهمنا معنى الجملة المكتوبة بالهامش.
examples.trans: Now we understand the meaning of the sentence written in the margin.

examples.text: كلام الجد دايما إله معنى عميق وحلو.
examples.trans: Grandfather's words always carry a deep and lovely meaning.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun of غامر (to venture); plural مغامرات.

examples.text: البحث عن الخريطة الضائعة كان مغامرة ممتعة.
examples.trans: Searching for the lost map was a fun adventure.

examples.text: الجد حكالنا عن مغامراته لما كان يبحر.
examples.trans: Grandfather told us about his adventures when he used to sail.

meanings.note: Used for remarks, annotations, or paying attention to details.

examples.trans: I have a small note on the work.

examples.text: سجلنا ملاحظة صغيرة عن نكهة قشر البرتقال.
examples.trans: We jotted down a short note about the orange peel flavour.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (pl. مهرجانات) used for street festivals, fairs, and cultural events.

examples.trans: We should put up a poster for the festival.
The street is full of people during the festival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موجودة, plural: موجودين).

examples.trans: Your glasses are right there on your forehead!
Tariq is down in the workshop.

meanings.note: Short adjective from root ن-ش-ط alongside نشيط; feminine نشطة.

examples.text: النحل الصبح بكون نشط وحوالين الزهر.
examples.trans: In the morning the bees are active around the blossoms.

examples.text: الفريق ضل نشط طول اليوم لحد ما حل اللغز.
examples.trans: The team stayed energetic all day until they solved the puzzle.

meanings.note: In نلفت نظرهم ('draw their eyes/attention'), pairs with لفت.

examples.trans: We don't want to catch the teacher's eye.
Your point of view is clear.

meanings.note: Contrasts with ليل ('nighttime'): بنور النهار = 'in broad daylight'.

examples.text: الشيش الأخضر طالع أحلى بكتير بنور النهار!
examples.trans: The green shutters look even lovelier in daylight!

examples.text: شتغلنا طول النهار وبالمسا شربنا شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: We worked all day long and in the evening had mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for feminine singular objects.

examples.trans: This girl is very smart.

examples.text: هاي الطريقة أسهل بكثير من اللي جربناها امبارح.
examples.trans: This method is much easier than the one we tried yesterday.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (مرة) from هب ('to blow'): هبة هوا ('a gust of wind'). Plural هبات.

examples.text: إجت هبة هوا قوية على الشرفة.
examples.trans: A strong gust of wind came onto the terrace.
The gusts of wind in autumn cool the weather down.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.text: هيك الحياة، يوم الك ويوم عليك.
examples.trans: Such is life, one day for you and one day against you.

examples.text: ما تحكي معه هيك قدام الناس، احكي معه على جنب.
examples.trans: Don't talk to him like that in front of people; speak to him privately.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Common urban Jordanian loanword from English weekend, alternating with عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

examples.trans: On the weekend we visit my grandfather and bake together.

examples.text: عندنا خطة حلوة للويكند الجاي بالقرية.
examples.trans: We have a nice plan for next weekend in the village.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
